title_en: Chen Qingzong v. Tingyang Village Group 1 and Tingyang Village Committee — dispute over distribution of land acquisition compensation
ruling_gist_en: According to Article 14 of the Land Administration Law and Article 26 of the Rural Land Contract Law, after a farmer who has contracted land moves to a small town and registers as a resident, his/her land contract management right may be retained or transferred according to law; if the land is expropriated, the farmer who has contracted the land is entitled to receive land expropriation compensation.

full_text_en:
**Chen Qingzong v. Tingyang Village Group No. 1 and Tingyang Village Villagers' Committee — Dispute over Distribution of Land Expropriation Compensation**

**Ruling Summary**

Pursuant to Article 14 of the Land Administration Law and Article 26 of the Land Contract Law, where a farmer who has contracted land settles in a small town, his or her land contractual management right may be retained or lawfully transferred; if the land is expropriated, the farmer who contracted the land is entitled to receive land expropriation compensation.

**Plaintiff:** Chen Qingzong, male, 33 years old, residing at Tingyang Village, Maxiang Town, Tong'an District, Xiamen City, Fujian Province.

**Defendant No. 1:** The First Villagers' Group of Tingyang Village Villagers' Committee, Maxiang Town, Tong'an District, Xiamen City, Fujian Province. Address: Tingyang Village, Maxiang Town, Tong'an District, Xiamen City.
**Representative:** Chen Zhongwen, Deputy Head of the Group.

**Defendant No. 2:** Tingyang Village Villagers' Committee, Maxiang Town, Tong'an District, Xiamen City, Fujian Province. Address: Tingyang Village, Maxiang Town, Tong'an District, Xiamen City.
**Legal Representative:** Chen Wufan, Director of the Villagers' Committee.

The plaintiff, Chen Qingzong, filed an action with the People's Court of Tong'an District, Xiamen City, Fujian Province, concerning a dispute over the distribution of land expropriation compensation with the First Villagers' Group of Tingyang Village Villagers' Committee, Maxiang Town, Tong'an District, Xiamen City (hereinafter referred to as "Tingyang Village Group No. 1") and Tingyang Village Villagers' Committee, Maxiang Town, Tong'an District, Xiamen City (hereinafter referred to as "Tingyang Village Villagers' Committee").

**Plaintiff's Allegations:** The plaintiff and his family of four were villagers of Defendant Tingyang Village Group No. 1. On January 5, 1996, the plaintiff, on behalf of his family, contracted 1.54 mu of land from Tingyang Village Group No. 1. This land contractual relationship was confirmed by the Land Contractual Management Right Certificate No. 066277 issued by the People's Government of Tong'an District, Xiamen City on December 31, 1998. On July 23, 2002, Defendant Tingyang Village Villagers' Committee entered into a land expropriation agreement with Xiamen Ruyi Food Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Ruyi Food Company"), whereby Ruyi Food Company expropriated 69.8 mu of dry land belonging to Tingyang Village, including 1.16 mu of land contracted by the plaintiff, by paying land compensation, resettlement fees, and young crop compensation to Tingyang Village Villagers' Committee. When Tingyang Village Group No. 1 distributed land compensation to the households whose contracted land had been expropriated, it did not distribute any amount to the plaintiff's family. The plaintiff requested that the court order Tingyang Village Group No. 1 and Tingyang Village Villagers' Committee to pay the plaintiff land expropriation compensation and resettlement fees totaling RMB 17,400.

**Defendant Tingyang Village Group No. 1's Defense:** Although the plaintiff and his family of four were originally villagers of this group and had contracted land in this group, since January 21, 2002, the plaintiff's family had moved their household registration out of this village and changed to non-agricultural household status. The land they originally contracted had been reallocated by this group to other villagers for contracting in accordance with the customary practice formed by village rules and folk conventions. After the group's land was expropriated, the land compensation, resettlement fees, etc., had all been fully distributed to the relevant farming households. Since after January 21, 2002, the plaintiff was no longer a member of this collective economic organization and had no contracted land that was expropriated, he had no right to request distribution of land expropriation compensation. Even if the plaintiff still held the Land Contractual Management Right Certificate issued in previous years, this fact could not be changed, and therefore his claim should be dismissed.

**Defendant Tingyang Village Villagers' Committee's Defense:** First, it supported the defense opinion of Tingyang Village Group No. 1. Second, in accordance with Article 5 of the Organic Law of the Villagers' Committees of the People's Republic of China, this Villagers' Committee, as the manager of the land collectively owned by the village farmers, merely carried out the formalities of signing the Land Expropriation Agreement with Ruyi Food Company in accordance with the wishes of the majority of the villagers of Tingyang Village Group No. 1. After the land was expropriated, the Villagers' Committee had handed over all the land compensation received to Tingyang Village Group No. 1, which was fully distributed by the villagers of that group according to their own decision-making plan. The Villagers' Committee did not withhold this sum, and therefore there was no dispute over distribution of land expropriation compensation between it and the plaintiff. The plaintiff's inclusion of this Villagers' Committee as a defendant in the lawsuit was erroneous. The court was requested to dismiss the plaintiff's claim in accordance with the law.

The People's Court of Tong'an District, Xiamen City found the following facts upon trial:

On January 5, 1996, the plaintiff, Chen Qingzong, on behalf of his family of four, in the capacity of a villager of Defendant Tingyang Village Group No. 1 (household category: agricultural household), entered into an agricultural production contract with Tingyang Village Group No. 1, contracting 1.16 mu of dry land and 0.38 mu of paddy field owned by the villagers of that group, totaling 1.54 mu. On December 31, 1998, the People's Government of Tong'an District, Xiamen City issued Land Contractual Management Right Certificate No. 066277 to Chen Qingzong, confirming the agricultural production contract relationship between Chen Qingzong's family and Tingyang Village Group No. 1. On January 21, 2002, Chen Qingzong's family moved to Yuekou, Biyue Village, Datong Town, Tong'an District, and their household category was changed to non-agricultural household. After Chen Qingzong's family moved out, Tingyang Village Group No. 1 reallocated the land originally contracted by Chen Qingzong's family to other villagers. On July 23, 2002, Ruyi Food Company entered into a Land Expropriation Agreement with Defendant Tingyang Village Villagers' Committee, expropriating 69.8 mu of dry land, including the 1.16 mu of land originally contracted by Chen Qingzong's family, and paid land compensation, resettlement fees, and young crop compensation. Tingyang Village Villagers' Committee and Tingyang Village Group No. 1 distributed the compensation proportionally to the households whose land had been expropriated, but did not distribute any to Chen Qingzong's family, thereby giving rise to the dispute. On July 24, 2002, Chen Qingzong moved his family's household registration back to Tingyang Village from Yuekou, Biyue Village, Datong Town, and the household category remained non-agricultural household. On March 11, 2003, Chen Qingzong filed the present action.

The People's Court of Tong'an District, Xiamen City held:

Article 71 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the "General Principles of Civil Law") provides: "Property ownership means the owner's rights to lawfully possess, use, profit from, and dispose of his property." Article 74, paragraph 2 provides: "Land collectively owned by farmers belongs to the village farmers' collective in accordance with the law, and is operated and managed by village agricultural production cooperatives or other agricultural collective economic organizations or villagers' committees. Land already belonging to the farmers' collective economic organizations at the township (town) level may be owned by the farmers' collective at the township (town) level." Although the plaintiff, Chen Qingzong, and his family were originally villagers of Defendant Tingyang Village Group No. 1, because their family had moved to Datong Town to reside on January 21, 2002, and their household category had changed to non-agricultural household, they had lost the right to contract land as agricultural personnel. It was reasonable for Tingyang Village Group No. 1 to lawfully recover the land contracted by Chen Qingzong's family. The rights enjoyed and obligations owed by Chen Qingzong's family in connection with the contracted land were extinguished accordingly. Thereafter, the contracted land was expropriated on July 23, 2002. Although Chen Qingzong's family moved back to Tingyang Village on July 24, 2002, they retained non-agricultural household status. Therefore, Chen Qingzong's request for Tingyang Village Group No. 1 and Defendant Tingyang Village Villagers' Committee to pay him land expropriation compensation and resettlement fees was unfounded and was not supported.

Accordingly, the People's Court of Tong'an District, Xiamen City rendered judgment on June 25, 2003:

The plaintiff's claim was dismissed.

The court acceptance fee for this case was RMB 706, to be borne by the plaintiff, Chen Qingzong.

After the first-instance judgment was announced, the plaintiff, Chen Qingzong, dissatisfied, appealed to the Xiamen Intermediate People's Court, Fujian Province. The grounds of appeal were:

1. The Land Contractual Management Right Certificate is the only legal document confirming the true and valid existence of a rural land contract relationship. In the first instance, the appellant had already adduced this evidence and the Agricultural Production Contract, fully proving that the appellant's family had a thirty-year contractual management right over the 1.16 mu of dry land of Tingyang Village Group No. 1. When the appellant moved out of Tingyang Village, he entrusted his contracted land to others for cultivation; it was not reallocated by the appellee, Tingyang Village Group No. 1, to others for cultivation. Although Tingyang Village Group No. 1 claimed that it had already recovered the appellant's contracted land, it did not produce any valid evidence. Under these circumstances, the first instance court, disregarding the true and valid legal document, completely accepted Tingyang Village Group No. 1's account and found that Tingyang Village Group No. 1 had already recovered the appellant's contracted land. This was an error in fact-finding.

2. According to Article 26 of the Rural Land Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the "Land Contract Law"), only when the contractor's entire family moves into a city with districts and changes to non-agricultural household status may the grantor recover the contracted land; conversely, if the contractor merely moves into a town or merely changes his household registration to non-agricultural household, the contracted land may not be recovered. Although the appellant's family moved to Datong Town to live for half a year at the beginning of 2002 and changed their household registration to non-agricultural household, because Datong Town had not yet established a corresponding social security mechanism, after the appellant and his wife arrived there, they had no stable job and lacked a stable source of income, thus being unable to make a living, and were forced to move back to their original residence in July of that year, intending to continue relying on the income from the contracted land for their livelihood. The appellant's family had worked and lived in the appellee's villagers' group all year round, relying on agricultural income as their main source of livelihood like other villagers, and therefore should have the right to participate in the distribution of land compensation and resettlement fees. Although their household registration category was changed to non-agricultural household for a short period of half a year, the appellant's farmer status had not changed. Starting from July 1 of this year, household registration management in Xiamen City began to abolish the distinction between agricultural and non-agricultural households. Now, those villagers who have actually received land compensation and resettlement fees are also residents, just like the appellant. This shows that although there was once a distinction in household registration categories, this cannot be the determining factor for receiving land compensation and resettlement fees. The appellees, Tingyang Village Villagers' Committee and Tingyang Village Group No. 1, have the responsibility to protect the lawful property rights and livelihood security rights of their members and should properly resettle the appellant's family and help them overcome their livelihood difficulties. However, Tingyang Village Villagers' Committee and Tingyang Village Group No. 1, on the ground that the appellant was no longer a farmer of this village, refused to give the appellant equal treatment as a villager, deprived the appellant's family of their basic right to survival, and pushed the appellant's family into livelihood difficulties. This practice clearly contravenes the law. The first instance court, ignoring the specific circumstances of the appellant and violating the fundamental spirit of the relevant legal provisions, simply found that it was reasonable for Tingyang Village Group No. 1 to recover the appellant's contracted land on the ground that the appellant's family had changed to non-agricultural household status, and accordingly dismissed the appellant's claim. This was an error in the application of law. The appellant requested that the second instance revoke the first-instance judgment and amend it to support the claim made by the appellant in the first instance.

**Appellee Tingyang Village Group No. 1's Response:** Since the implementation of the production responsibility system, the contracted land of the villagers in this group was adjusted once a year according to the changes in the population of each household, and later changed to once every two years. This adjustment method had continued for twenty years and had become the customary form of land adjustment and distribution agreed upon by the villagers of this group. Although at the end of 1998, land extension contracting was implemented and Land Contractual Management Right Certificates were issued to each household, the villagers of this group had always continued to adjust and distribute contracted land according to the original customary practice. This customary form of contracted land distribution had not been objected to by all villagers (including the appellant before he moved his household registration out) and constituted a village rule and folk convention. It was based on the population composition ratio of this group's villagers and this village rule and folk convention that the appellant, according to the customary practice at that time, obtained the corresponding share of contracted land for his family of four. After January 21, 2002, when the appellant's household registration was moved out of this village, in accordance with the village rule and folk convention of this group, his originally contracted land was re-adjusted and re-contracted by all the villagers of this group. After the right to use all 69.8 mu of land of this group was transferred to Ruyi Food Company at a standard of RMB 15,000 per mu, the RMB 1,047,000 in land compensation and RMB 168,792.40 in compensation for above-ground objects obtained had all been paid to the farming households whose contracted land had been expropriated. Since the appellant was not a villager of this group and had no contracted land that was expropriated this time, he had no right to request distribution of land expropriation compensation. The first-instance judgment was correct and should be affirmed.

**Appellee Tingyang Village Villagers' Committee** supported the response of Tingyang Village Group No. 1.

The Xiamen Intermediate People's Court found the following facts upon trial: The finding in the first-instance judgment that "after Chen Qingzong's family moved out, Tingyang Village Group No. 1 reallocated the land originally contracted by Chen Qingzong's family to other villagers" was not supported by corresponding evidence and should not be confirmed; the time when Ruyi Food Company paid the land compensation, resettlement fees, and young crop compensation should be September 1, 2002. Apart from this, the other facts found in the first instance were confirmed as true. It was further found that before the land was expropriated, the appellee had used a "New Village Land Expropriation Voting Form" to solicit opinions on the expropriation from villagers who had contracted land within the scope of expropriation, household by household, and the appellant, Chen Qingzong, signed the voting form to consent to the expropriation.

**The Xiamen Intermediate People's Court held:**

Article 4 of the General Principles of Civil Law provides: "Civil activities shall adhere to the principles of voluntariness, fairness, compensation for equal value, and good faith." Article 14, paragraph 1 of the Land Administration Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the "Land Administration Law") provides: "Land collectively owned by farmers shall be contracted and managed by members of the collective economic organization for engaging in crop cultivation, forestry, animal husbandry, and fishery production. The term of land contractual management shall be 30 years. The grantor and the contractor shall conclude a contract specifying the rights and obligations of both parties. Farmers who contract and manage the land have the obligation to protect the land and use it rationally in accordance with the purposes stipulated in the contract. The farmers' land contractual management right shall be protected by law." Paragraph 2 provides: "During the term of land contractual management, any appropriate adjustment of the contracted land between individual contractors must be approved by at least two-thirds of the members of the villagers' meeting or by at least two-thirds of the villagers' representatives, and shall be reported to the township (town) people's government and the agricultural administrative department of the county people's government for approval." Article 26, paragraph 1 of the Land Contract Law provides: "During the term of the contract, the grantor may not recover the contracted land." Paragraph 2 provides: "During the term of the contract, if the contractor's entire family moves to a small town and settles there, the contractor's land contractual management right shall be retained or the contractor shall be allowed to lawfully transfer the land contractual management right according to the contractor's wishes." Paragraph 3 provides: "During the term of the contract, if the contractor's entire family moves to a city with districts and changes to non-agricultural household registration, the contractor shall return the contracted farmland and grassland to the grantor. If the contractor fails to return them, the grantor may recover the contracted farmland and grassland."

The settlement of farmers in cities is a social development trend. However, the social security system suitable for the characteristics of small towns is still being actively explored and established. At present, after farmers enter small towns, regardless of whether their household registration category changes, they cannot yet be guaranteed to enjoy basic livelihood security. The reason why the Land Contract Law stipulates that "if the contractor's entire family moves to a small town and settles there, the contractor's land contractual management right shall be retained or the contractor shall be allowed to lawfully transfer the land contractual management right according to the contractor's wishes" is mainly because land is the basic livelihood security for farmers. If their contracted land is recovered when the basic livelihood security for farmers after they enter small towns has not yet been implemented, it may cause them to face livelihood difficulties.

Before January 21, 2002, the appellant, Chen Qingzong, and his family resided in Tingyang Village and were villagers of the appellees, Tingyang Village Villagers' Committee and Tingyang Village Group No. 1. The Land Contractual Management Right Certificate proves that Chen Qingzong's family contracted land in Tingyang Village Group No. 1, with the contract period ending on December 31, 2028. The "New Village Land Expropriation Voting Form" signed by Chen Qingzong to consent to the expropriation not only proves that part of the land contracted by Chen Qingzong fell within the scope of this expropriation, but also proves that before the land was expropriated, Tingyang Village Villagers' Committee and Tingyang Village Group No. 1 recognized that Chen Qingzong had a contractual management right over this portion of land. During the contract term, Chen Qingzong's family's land contractual management right should be protected by law. During the period from January 22 to July 24, 2002, although Chen Qingzong's family's household registration was moved out of Tingyang Village and changed to non-agricultural household, they did not move to a city with districts, but to a small town. During this period, in respect of the land contracted by Chen Qingzong's family in Tingyang Village, their land contractual management right should have been retained or they should have been allowed to lawfully transfer the land contractual management right according to their wishes. Tingyang Village Villagers' Committee and Tingyang Village Group No. 1 had no evidence to prove that the dry land contracted by Chen Qingzong had been reallocated to other villagers before the expropriation. Even if such a fact could be proved, this practice would not be protected by law because it does not comply with Article 14, paragraph 2 of the Land Administration Law and Article 26, paragraphs 1 and 2 of the Land Contract Law. Therefore, Chen Qingzong's claim for land expropriation compensation (i.e., RMB 15,000 per mu x 1.16 mu = RMB 17,400) compared with the standard applicable to other villagers was in accordance with the law and should be supported. The first-instance judgment was based on unclear facts and erroneous application of law and should be amended in accordance with the law.

Accordingly, in accordance with Article 64, paragraph 1 and Article 153, paragraph 1, subparagraph (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Xiamen Intermediate People's Court rendered judgment on December 11, 2003:

1. The civil judgment of the first instance was reversed;
2. The appellees, Tingyang Village Group No. 1 and Tingyang Village Villagers' Committee, were ordered to pay the appellant, Chen Qingzong, land compensation of RMB 17,400 within 10 days from the effective date of this judgment.

The court acceptance fees for the first and second instances, each RMB 706, shall be borne by the appellees, Tingyang Village Group No. 1 and Tingyang Village Villagers' Committee.
